mainTopic: The warning before a court oath (אימת שבועה) and the גמרא's analysis of it
overview: This amud continues the warning that בית דין gives a person before he takes an oath. A ברייתא lists the ways a false oath is harsher than other sins. The world trembled when 'לא תשא' was said, the פסוק says 'לא ינקה', and the punishment reaches the sinner's family and even the whole world. It also comes immediately and destroys even wood and stones. If the person still insists on swearing, the court tells him the oath goes by the meaning of המקום and the בית דין, as משה did when he made ישראל swear. That oath also bound future generations, future גרים and later מצוות like מקרא מגילה. The גמרא then goes back over the ברייתא line by line. It explains that שבועת הדיינין may be said in any language, and that the world trembled because of 'לא ינקה', which is told apart from רבי אלעזר's teaching about תשובה. It also explains that for other sins the family gets a different punishment, while for a false oath it gets the sinner's own. The amud ends with a challenge from 'כל ישראל ערבים זה בזה', and the answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: The whole world trembled at 'Do not take God's name in vain'
steps.stepSummary: The warning tells the swearer that the entire world shook when הקדוש ברוך הוא said 'לא תשא' at סיני.
steps.simpleTranslation: [Know] that the whole world shook at the moment הקדוש ברוך הוא said at סיני: 'Do not take the name of ה׳ your God in vain.'
steps.whatsHappening: The warning given to the person about to swear continues here. The first point is how frightening this sin is: the whole world shook when it was forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Of all the דברות, this one is singled out as having shaken the world. The goal is to scare the swearer away from a false oath. This sets up the list of ways a false oath is harsher than other sins.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Do not take (God's name in vain)', the third of the עשרת הדברות
the warning that makes a person fear the oath before swearing

phrases.english: that the entire world trembled

phrases.aramaic: בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁאָמַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בְּסִינַי
phrases.english: at the time the Holy One, Blessed be He, said at Sinai:

phrases.aramaic: ״לֹא תִשָּׂא אֶת שֵׁם ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ לַשָּׁוְא״.
phrases.english: "You shall not take the name of the Lord your God in vain."
phrases.notes: שמות 20:7

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the warning that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A false oath is so serious that the whole world trembled when it was forbidden at סיני.

steps.title: Other sins can be cleared, but this one 'will not be cleared'
steps.stepSummary: For other sins the פסוק says 'ונקה' (He clears), but for a false oath it says 'לא ינקה' (He will not clear).
steps.simpleTranslation: For all other sins in the תורה it says 'and He clears', but here it says 'He will not clear'.
steps.whatsHappening: The warning gives a second difference: other sins can be forgiven, but the פסוק about a false oath says ה׳ will not clear the sinner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The contrast is built on the word נקה. In the י״ג מידות the תורה says 'ונקה', which shows forgiveness for sins in general. The פסוק of 'לא תשא' ends with 'לא ינקה', which singles this sin out as one that is not cleared the same way.

keyTerms.meaning: 'and He clears', a word of forgiveness

phrases.english: And regarding all the transgressions in the Torah,
it is stated about them: "And He clears";
phrases.notes: שמות 34:7, from the י״ג מידות.

phrases.english: but here it is stated: "He will not clear."
phrases.notes: This is the end of the same פסוק of לא תשא: 'for ה׳ will not clear one who takes His name in vain.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכׇל עֲבֵירוֹת שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה נֶאֱמַר בָּהֶן וְנַקֵּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second point to the warning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Unlike other sins, a false oath is described as 'not cleared'.

steps.title: The punishment reaches the sinner's family too
steps.stepSummary: For other sins only the sinner is punished, but for a false oath his family is punished too. This is learned from 'בשרך' (your flesh), which means relatives.
steps.simpleTranslation: For other sins, punishment is taken only from the sinner. Here it is taken from him and his family, because the פסוק says 'Do not let your mouth cause your flesh to sin', and 'your flesh' means your relative, as it says 'do not hide from your own flesh.'
steps.whatsHappening: The warning adds a third difference: a false oath brings punishment on the sinner's family as well. It proves this from a פסוק in קהלת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says a sin of the mouth (an oath) brings guilt on 'your flesh'. To show that 'flesh' means family, the ברייתא brings a פסוק in ישעיהו where 'your flesh' clearly means a relative. So the damage of a false oath spreads past the sinner himself.

phrases.english: And for all the transgressions in the Torah, punishment is exacted from him alone;
but here, from him and from his family,
as it is stated: "Do not allow your mouth
to bring your flesh into sin."
phrases.notes: קהלת 5:5

phrases.english: And 'his flesh' means nothing other than his relative,
as it is stated: "And do not hide yourself from your own flesh."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכׇל עֲבֵירוֹת שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה נִפְרָעִין מִמֶּנּוּ וְכָאן מִמֶּנּוּ וּמִמִּשְׁפַּחְתּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third, wider consequence of a false oath.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For a false oath, punishment reaches the sinner's family too, since 'בשרך' means relatives.

steps.title: The punishment reaches the whole world
steps.stepSummary: For a false oath, punishment reaches even the whole world, learned from the פסוק in הושע that begins 'אלה וכחש'.
steps.simpleTranslation: For other sins, punishment is taken only from the sinner. Here it is taken from him and from the whole world, as it says: 'Swearing and lying...'
steps.whatsHappening: The warning gives its widest point: a false oath can bring suffering on the whole world. The source is the פסוק in הושע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in הושע lists swearing falsely together with other sins and then says the land mourns and all its people suffer. From this the warning learns that the world as a whole pays for this sin. This sets up the question in the next step.

phrases.english: And for all the transgressions in the Torah, punishment is exacted from him alone;
but here, from him and from the entire world,
as it is stated: "Swearing and lying."
phrases.notes: הושע 4:2. The פסוק goes on to list murder, stealing and adultery, and the next פסוק says the land mourns.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Widens the punishment from the family to the whole world.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A false oath brings punishment on the entire world.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the most extreme claim in the warning, so the גמרא now checks the proof behind it.

steps.title: Maybe the world is punished only when all the listed sins are done
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the proof: the פסוק in הושע lists many sins, so maybe the world suffers only when all of them are committed.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say that this happens only when he does all of them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from הושע. Since the פסוק lists several sins together, perhaps only all of them together bring punishment on the world.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The weak spot is that the פסוק mentions swearing alongside murder, theft and adultery. If the land's mourning comes from the whole list, a false oath alone would not be enough to harm the world. This sets up the answer in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: 'but say', the opening of a challenge

phrases.english: But say: not until he commits all of them!
phrases.notes: 'All of them' means all the sins listed in that פסוק in הושע.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof from הושע given in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a false oath alone brings punishment on the whole world.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק lists several sins together, so the punishment may depend on all of them combined.

steps.title: A פסוק in ירמיהו shows the oath alone is enough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the challenge. ירמיהו says 'because of swearing the land mourns', and הושע uses the same word, 'the land mourns'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Don't think that. It says: 'Because of swearing the land mourns', and it says: 'Therefore the land mourns and everyone who lives in it suffers.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge with a פסוק in ירמיהו that blames the land's mourning on swearing alone. The same word 'mourn' appears in הושע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ירמיהו ties the land's mourning to swearing by itself, without the other sins. Because הושע uses the same word, 'mourns', we learn that the mourning there can also come from the oath alone. So a false oath by itself brings suffering on the world.

keyTerms.meaning: 'don't think that', the idea is rejected

steps.whatToRemember: A false oath is uniquely severe. It shook the world at סיני, it is 'not cleared', and its punishment reaches the sinner's family and even the whole world. The oath alone is enough for that, as ירמיהו shows.

phrases.english: This should not enter your mind,
as it is written: "Because of swearing the land mourns,"
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 23:10

phrases.english: and it is written: "Therefore the land mourns,
and everyone who dwells in it languishes."
phrases.notes: This is הושע 4:3, the very next פסוק. Both פסוקים use the same word, 'mourns'.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ דִּכְתִיב מִפְּנֵי אָלָה אָבְלָה הָאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings an extra פסוק that links the shared word 'mourn' to swearing alone.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The world suffers only when all the sins in הושע are committed together.
steps.terutzMaskana: Swearing falsely alone makes the land mourn, so the whole world is punished for it.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A false oath by itself brings punishment on the whole world.

steps.title: A false oath is punished immediately
steps.stepSummary: With other sins, a person's merit can delay punishment for two or three generations. A false oath is punished right away, as the פסוק in זכריה shows.
steps.simpleTranslation: For all other sins in the תורה, if the person has merit, his punishment is held off for two or three generations. Here it is collected from him immediately, as it says: 'I cause it to go forth, says ה׳ of hosts, and it shall enter the house of the thief and the house of the one who swears falsely by My name. It shall stay inside his house and consume it, with its wood and its stones.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds one more way a false oath is worse than other sins: its punishment is not delayed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 2 to 4 compared a false oath to other sins in how strict the punishment is and who suffers. Now the comparison is about timing. Merit can hold off punishment for other sins, but not for a false oath. The proof is the פסוק in זכריה, which the next step explains word by word.

keyTerms.meaning: Merit, good deeds that protect a person
They hold off or suspend the punishment

phrases.english: And all the other transgressions in the Torah:
if he has merit,
they hold off his punishment for two or three generations;
but here, punishment is collected from him immediately,
as it says: 'I cause it to go forth, says the Lord of hosts,
phrases.notes: זכריה 5:4. 'It' refers to the curse.

phrases.english: and it shall enter the house of the thief
and the house of the one who swears falsely by My name,
and it shall stay inside his house and consume it,
along with its wood and its stones.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכׇל עֲבֵירוֹת שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה אִם יֵשׁ לוֹ זְכוּת תּוֹלִין לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of ways a false oath is worse than other sins, now looking at timing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Merit delays punishment for other sins, but a false oath is punished immediately.

steps.title: Explaining the words of the פסוק in זכריה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains the פסוק piece by piece: 'I cause it to go forth' means immediately. The 'thief' is someone who tricks a person into an oath. 'Swears falsely' means just what it says. 'Wood and stones' teaches that a false oath destroys even what fire and water cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'I cause it to go forth' means immediately. 'And it shall enter the house of the thief' refers to someone who deceives people: he has no money owed to him by his friend, yet he claims it and makes him swear. 'And the house of the one who swears falsely by My name' means just what it says. From 'It shall stay inside his house and consume it, with its wood and its stones' you learn that a false oath destroys things that even fire and water do not destroy.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא goes through the פסוק it just quoted and explains each part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'הוצאתיה' is the source for 'immediately' in step 7. The 'thief' is not a regular thief. He is someone who makes a false claim and forces the other person to take an oath for nothing, so he shares in the punishment. The ending shows how strong the punishment is: a false oath consumes even stones, which fire and water cannot destroy.

keyTerms.meaning: He makes a claim against him and makes him swear
Just as it sounds, the plain meaning

steps.confusionAlert: The 'thief' in this פסוק is not someone who takes objects. He is the person who makes a false claim and forces an innocent man to swear.

phrases.english: 'I cause it to go forth' means immediately.
'And it shall enter the house of the thief':
this is one who deceives people;
his friend does not owe him any money,
yet he claims it from him and makes him swear.
'And the house of the one who swears falsely by My name' means just what it says.
'And it shall stay inside his house and consume it,
along with its wood and its stones':
from this you have learned

phrases.aramaic: דְּבָרִים שֶׁאֵין אֵשׁ וּמַיִם מְכַלִּין אוֹתָן,
phrases.english: that things which fire and water do not destroy,
a false oath does destroy.
phrases.notes: Stones are the example: fire and water can't wipe them out, but a false oath can.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the פסוק quoted in step 7 word by word.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A false oath is punished at once. The one who forces a needless oath shares the punishment, and the destruction reaches even wood and stones.

steps.title: If he refuses or agrees to swear
steps.stepSummary: After the warning, if he says he won't swear, the court lets him go right away. If he says he will swear, the people present tell each other to move away from the wicked.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he says, 'I won't swear,' they release him right away. If he says, 'I will swear,' the people standing there say to each other: 'Please move away from the tents of these wicked men.'
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the warning is finished, the ברייתא describes the two ways the person can respond.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he refuses, no oath is taken and the case ends at once. Since he would not swear, he pays. If he insists on swearing even after hearing such a harsh warning, the people there treat him as suspect. They quote the words said about קורח's group: stay away from the wicked so you are not caught up in their punishment.

keyTerms.meaning: They release him, here meaning from the oath

phrases.english: If he says: 'I will not swear,'
they release him immediately.
phrases.notes: He is let go without an oath. Since he won't swear, he pays the claim.

phrases.english: And if he says: 'I will swear,'
the people standing there say to each other:
'Please move away from the tents of
these wicked men, etc.'
phrases.notes: במדבר 16:26. משה said this about קורח's group.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם אָמַר אֵינִי נִשְׁבָּע פּוֹטְרִין אוֹתוֹ מִיָּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the warning is complete, the ברייתא tells what happens depending on his answer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Refusing ends the matter at once. Agreeing to swear makes the people present distance themselves from him.

steps.title: The oath follows the court's meaning, not his
steps.stepSummary: When the court gives him the oath, they tell him it goes by the meaning of המקום and the בית דין, not by his own private meaning.
steps.simpleTranslation: When they make him swear, they tell him: 'Know that we are not making you swear according to your own understanding, but according to the understanding of המקום and of the בית דין.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא tells us the last thing the judges say as they actually give the oath.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might try to swear with a hidden private meaning in mind, so that his words are technically true to him. The court shuts this down: the oath means what הקב״ה and the judges understand it to mean. Any secret meaning he has in mind does not count.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'the Place': a name for הקב״ה
According to the understanding or intent of

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basis for the הלכה that a court oath goes by the court's intent, so a person cannot escape it with hidden meanings.

phrases.english: And when they make him swear, they say to him:
Know

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא עַל דַּעְתְּךָ אָנוּ מַשְׁבִּיעִין אוֹתְךָ,
phrases.english: that we are not making you swear according to your own understanding,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא עַל דַּעַת הַמָּקוֹם וְעַל דַּעַת בֵּית דִּין.
phrases.english: but according to the understanding of the Omnipresent and the understanding of the court.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּכְשֶׁמַּשְׁבִּיעִין אוֹתוֹ אוֹמְרִים לוֹ הֱוֵי יוֹדֵעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues from the case where he agrees to swear, describing how the oath is actually given.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A court oath is taken according to the intent of המקום and the בית דין, not the swearer's private intent.

steps.title: Support from משה רבינו
steps.stepSummary: משה did the same thing when he made ישראל swear. He said the oath was by הקב״ה's understanding and his own, not theirs, as shown by 'ולא אתכם לבדכם'.
steps.simpleTranslation: We find this with משה רבינו. When he made ישראל swear, he told them: 'Know that I am not making you swear according to your understanding, but according to the understanding of המקום and my understanding,' as it says: 'And not with you alone...'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings proof for the rule in step 10 from how משה gave ישראל an oath.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה also told the people that their oath went by his meaning and הקב״ה's, not theirs. The פסוק 'not with you alone' is read here as 'not by your understanding alone.' This shows that the court in step 10 is following משה's example.

keyTerms.meaning: For so we find, introducing a supporting example

steps.whatToRemember: A false oath is uniquely harsh in several ways: it is 'not cleared', its punishment reaches the family and the world, it is punished immediately, and it destroys even stones. An oath in court always goes by the meaning of הקב״ה and the בית דין, just as משה did.

phrases.english: For so we find with Moses our teacher,
when he made the Jewish people swear,
he said to them: Know

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא עַל דַּעְתְּכֶם אֲנִי מַשְׁבִּיעַ אֶתְכֶם,
phrases.english: that I am not making you swear according to your understanding,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא עַל דַּעַת הַמָּקוֹם וְעַל דַּעְתִּי;
phrases.english: but according to the understanding of the Omnipresent and my understanding;
as it says: 'And not with you alone, etc.'
phrases.notes: דברים 29:13. Here it's read as 'not by your understanding alone.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support for the rule in step 10 that an oath follows the court's intent.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that an oath is taken according to the intent of המקום and the one giving the oath, not the swearer's intent.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משה's oath to ישראל, with the פסוק 'ולא אתכם לבדכם' (דברים 29:13).

steps.title: The oath also covered future generations and converts
steps.stepSummary: From 'את אשר ישנו פה' we would only know about the people standing at הר סיני. 'ואת אשר איננו' adds future generations and future גרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'With whoever is here.' From this I would only know about the people who stood at הר סיני. How do we know the oath also covers later generations and people who will convert in the future? The פסוק says: 'and with whoever is not here.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא keeps reading the same section of פסוקים about the oath משה made ישראל take. It learns that the oath also covers people who were not there yet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half of the פסוק, 'whoever is here,' sounds like it only covers the people who were present. The second half, 'whoever is not here,' must be adding someone else. That means Jews of later generations and future גרים are also bound by the oath.

keyTerms.meaning: 'I only know...' (a limited reading that a later phrase will widen)
'the פסוק teaches' (introduces the proof from the פסוק)

phrases.english: "But with whoever is here"
phrases.notes: דברים 29:14

phrases.english: I would only know about
those standing at Mount Sinai;
the generations that will come
and converts who will convert in the future – from where do we know?
The verse says: "And with whoever is not here."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא's reading of the same section of פסוקים about משה's oath, moving on to the next פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The oath at ערבות מואב binds future generations and future גרים too, learned from 'ואת אשר איננו'.

steps.title: The oath also covered מצוות added later, like reading the מגילה
steps.stepSummary: We might think the oath only covered מצוות accepted at הר סיני. 'קיימו וקבלו' teaches that later מצוות like מקרא מגילה were already accepted back then.
steps.simpleTranslation: I would only know about the מצוות they accepted at הר סיני. How do we know about מצוות that would be added later, like reading the מגילה? The פסוק says: 'They upheld and accepted.' This means they upheld what they had already accepted long before.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא widens the oath a second way. Not only more people, but also more מצוות, even ones that came later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In מגילת אסתר the order is 'upheld' and then 'accepted,' which seems backwards. The ברייתא reads it as: in the days of אסתר they upheld something they had already accepted at the oath long before. So even a later מצוה like מקרא מגילה was included in the original oath.

keyTerms.meaning: מצוות that would be newly added in the future
reading the מגילת אסתר on פורים

steps.whatToRemember: משה's oath covered every Jew, present or future, and every מצוה, even ones added later like מקרא מגילה.

phrases.english: And I would only know about a מצוה
that they took upon themselves from Mount Sinai;
מצוות that would be newly added in the future,
such as reading the Megillah – from where do we know?
The verse says: "They upheld and accepted" –
phrases.notes: אסתר 9:27

phrases.english: they upheld what they had already accepted.
phrases.notes: 'Already' means back at the time of משה's oath, long before אסתר's time.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין לִי אֶלָּא מִצְוָה שֶׁקִּיבְּלוּ עֲלֵיהֶם מֵהַר סִינַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same 'אין לי אלא... מנין' pattern as Step 12, now widening which מצוות the oath covers instead of which people.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מצוות added later, like מקרא מגילה, were already included in the original oath, learned from 'קיימו וקבלו'.

steps.title: What does 'it too is said in its language' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to a phrase in the ברייתא about the judges' oath and asks what it means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does the ברייתא mean when it says: 'It too is said in its language'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the side discussion about the oath at ערבות מואב and returns to the ברייתא about שבועת הדיינין. It asks what one phrase means, which sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'it too' suggest the judges' oath is being added to some known list, but the ברייתא never says which list. 'In its language' is also unclear. The גמרא wants both explained.

keyTerms.meaning: 'it too' (adds something to an existing list)

phrases.english: What is meant by "it too
is said in its language"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side discussion about the oath at ערבות מואב (Steps 11-13) and goes back to the ברייתא's rules for שבועת הדיינין.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What list the judges' oath is being added to with 'אף היא', and what 'בלשונה' means.

steps.title: The judges' oath joins the list of things that may be said in any language
steps.stepSummary: A משנה lists things that may be said in any language. The ברייתא adds שבועת הדיינין to that list.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: These may be said in any language: the section said to a סוטה, וידוי מעשר, קריאת שמע, תפילה, ברכת המזון, the oath of testimony, and the oath about a deposit. And the ברייתא also says: the judges' oath, it too may be said in its language.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by pointing to a משנה with a list of things that do not have to be said in לשון הקודש. 'It too' means the judges' oath joins that list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now both unclear parts make sense. 'It too' refers to this known list. 'In its language' means in any language the person understands, just like everything else on the list.

keyTerms.meaning: the section the כהן says to a סוטה
the declaration that one gave his מעשרות properly
the oath that the judges give

steps.whatToRemember: שבועת הדיינין, like שבועת העדות and שבועת הפקדון, may be said in any language the person understands.
steps.confusionAlert: 'In its language' does not mean the judges' oath has its own special language. It means it may be said in any language.

phrases.english: As we learned in a Mishnah:
phrases.notes: This משנה is in סוטה 32a.

phrases.english: These are said in any language –
the section said to a Sotah,
the declaration of tithes,
the reading of Shema, and prayer,
and Grace after Meals,
and the oath of testimony,
and the oath about a deposit.
And it also says:
phrases.notes: 'It' is our ברייתא, which adds one more item to the משנה's list.

phrases.english: the oath of the judges –
it too is said in its language.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of Step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'אף היא' adds the judges' oath to the משנה's list in סוטה of things that may be said in any language, so 'בלשונה' means in any language.

steps.title: Why did the world tremble at 'Do not swear falsely'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's line that the world trembled when 'לא תשא' was said, and asks for the reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא said: the judges tell the swearer, 'Know that the whole world shook when הקב״ה said, Do not take ה׳'s name in vain.' What is the reason the world shook specifically then?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to another phrase from the ברייתא about the judges' warning and asks why this commandment made the world tremble. This sets up the next few steps, where possible answers are tried.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא singles out 'לא תשא' as the moment the world shook. The גמרא wants to know what is special about this commandment that would justify that claim.

keyTerms.meaning: 'You shall not take [ה׳'s name in vain]', the ban on false or empty oaths

phrases.english: The Master said: They say to him:
Be aware
that the entire world trembled
at the time that the Holy One, Blessed be He, said:

phrases.aramaic: ״לֹא תִשָּׂא אֶת שֵׁם ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ לַשָּׁוְא״.
phrases.english: "You shall not take the name of ה׳ your God in vain."
phrases.notes: שמות 20:7

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to another phrase of the same ברייתא to explain it
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the world trembled specifically when 'לא תשא' was given

steps.title: Not because it was given at סיני
steps.stepSummary: A first suggestion, that it was because it was given at סיני, is rejected because all of the עשרת הדברות were given there.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say the reason is that it was given at סיני, that cannot be, because all the Ten Commandments were given there too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one possible answer and knocks it down right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being said at סיני is not special to 'לא תשא'. All of the עשרת הדברות share that, so it cannot explain why this one commandment made the world tremble.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If you say', which introduces a suggestion that will be rejected

phrases.english: If you say it is because it was given at סיני,
the Ten Commandments were also given there!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers and rejects a first answer to the question
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that being given at סיני is the reason
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: That feature is shared by all of the עשרת הדברות, so it is not unique

steps.title: Not because it is more severe than other sins
steps.stepSummary: A second suggestion, that 'לא תשא' is extra severe, is rejected by a source that places it with the severe sins, not above them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Maybe it is because this sin is so severe? But is it more severe than others? We learned: light sins are ordinary positive and negative מצוות, except 'לא תשא'. Severe sins are those punished with כרת or a בית דין death penalty, and 'לא תשא' is counted with them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second answer, severity, and rejects it using a teaching that lists different levels of sins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source shows 'לא תשא' is heavier than a regular לאו, but only on the same level as כרת and מיתות בית דין. Since other sins are just as severe, severity alone does not explain why the world trembled at this one.

keyTerms.meaning: sins punished with כרת, being cut off
death penalties given by a court

steps.confusionAlert: The source does make 'לא תשא' serious, so the point is not that it is light. The point is that it is only equal to other severe sins, not more than them.

phrases.english: And rather, is it because it is severe?
But is it more severe?!
But didn't we learn: These are the light sins:
positive and negative מצוות,
except for "You shall not take."
Severe ones: these are sins punished with כרת
and court death penalties,
and "You shall not take" is with them!
phrases.notes: It is counted together with them, not above them, so it is no more severe than they are.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer after the first was rejected, and rejects it too
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that extra severity is the reason
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A source lists 'לא תשא' on the same level as כרת and מיתות בית דין, not above them

steps.title: The ברייתא's own reason: 'He will not clear'
steps.stepSummary: The reason is what the ברייתא itself says: other sins have 'ונקה' (He clears), but here the Torah says 'לא ינקה' (He will not clear).
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the reason is as the ברייתא teaches: about all other sins in the Torah it says 'and He will clear', but here it says 'He will not clear'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question using the reason the ברייתא itself gives later on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What makes 'לא תשא' unique is the type of punishment, not where it was said or how severe it is. For other sins there is a way to be cleared, but here the פסוק says ה׳ will not clear the sinner.

keyTerms.meaning: 'and He will clear', meaning He forgives or cleans away the sin
'He will not clear', meaning no forgiveness

phrases.english: Rather, it is as the reason is taught:
And for all the sins in the Torah,
it is said about them "and He will clear,"
but here it is said "He will not clear."
phrases.notes: שמות 20:7, the end of the 'לא תשא' פסוק.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the accepted answer after two suggestions were rejected
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The difference is 'ונקה' for other sins versus 'לא ינקה' for 'לא תשא'

steps.title: But other sins also say 'He will not clear'
steps.stepSummary: The answer is challenged: a פסוק about all sins says 'ונקה לא ינקה', so 'לא ינקה' is said about other sins too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it really true that 'He will not clear' is not said about other sins? But it is written: 'He clears, He will not clear'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave, pointing to a פסוק that uses 'לא ינקה' for all sins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer depended on 'לא ינקה' being found only by 'לא תשא'. The פסוק in the י״ג מדות contains both 'ונקה' and 'לא ינקה' about sins in general, which seems to erase the difference.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But isn't it written?', which brings a פסוק to challenge
'He clears, He will not clear', a phrase from the י״ג מדות

phrases.english: And for all the sins in the Torah,
is "He will not clear" not said about them?!
But it is written: "He clears, He will not clear"!
phrases.notes: שמות 34:7. The same פסוק has both words, and it talks about sins in general.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכׇל עֲבֵירוֹת שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה לֹא נֶאֱמַר בָּהֶן ״לֹא יְנַקֶּה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in the previous step
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that only 'לא תשא' has 'לא ינקה'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמות 34:7 says 'ונקה לא ינקה' about sins in general, so 'לא ינקה' is not unique to 'לא תשא'

steps.title: That verse teaches about people who repent
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'ונקה לא ינקה' is not saying all sins are never cleared. It is needed for רבי אלעזר's teaching: ה׳ clears those who do תשובה and does not clear those who don't.
steps.simpleTranslation: That verse is needed for the teaching of רבי אלעזר, as it was taught: רבי אלעזר says: It is impossible to say 'and He clears,' since it already says 'He will not clear.' It is impossible to say 'He will not clear,' since it already says 'and He clears.' How do these fit together? He clears those who repent, and does not clear those who do not repent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 20. The words 'ונקה לא ינקה' in that general פסוק have a different job: they teach the difference between someone who does תשובה and someone who doesn't.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge said 'לא ינקה' is also said about other sins, so it cannot be what makes a false oath special. The answer is that in the general פסוק, the two words 'ונקה' and 'לא ינקה' seem to contradict each other, so רבי אלעזר explains them as two groups of people. That means the general פסוק never says that other sins are 'not cleared' outright. Only for לא תשא does the Torah say 'לא ינקה' with no 'ונקה' alongside it.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed for, meaning this פסוק is used to teach something else
How do these fit together?, used to settle two sources that seem to clash
Those who repent, who do תשובה

phrases.english: That verse is needed
phrases.notes: "That verse" is the general פסוק from step 20 that says 'ונקה לא ינקה' (שמות 34:7).

phrases.english: for the teaching of Rabbi Elazar
as it was taught: Rabbi Elazar says:
It is impossible to say "and He clears,"
since it already says "He will not clear";
it is impossible to say "He will not clear,"
since it already says "and He clears."
How do these fit together?
He clears those who repent,
and does not clear those who do not repent.

steps.whatToRemember: The general פסוק 'ונקה לא ינקה' is about תשובה. Only for לא תשא is there a plain 'לא ינקה', so the original answer in step 19 stands.
steps.whyThisMatters: רבי אלעזר's teaching is a well-known source that תשובה brings forgiveness.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 20 by reassigning the general פסוק to a different teaching.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigning the source: the challenging פסוק is needed for a different teaching.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'לא ינקה' in the general פסוק means other sins are also not cleared, so a false oath is not unique.
steps.terutzMaskana: The general פסוק separates people who repent from people who don't. Only לא תשא has an unqualified 'לא ינקה'.

steps.title: The ברייתא says the family is punished for a false oath
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the ברייתא: for all other sins only the sinner is punished, but here his משפחה is punished too.
steps.simpleTranslation: For all sins in the Torah, punishment is taken from him; but here, from him and from his family.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings up the next line of the ברייתא so it can examine it. This is a setup for the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is another way the ברייתא says a false oath is more serious than other sins, after the trembling at סיני and 'לא ינקה'. Here the difference is not about forgiveness but about who gets punished. The גמרא will now test whether it is really true that other sins never affect the family.

keyTerms.meaning: Punishment is taken, they collect payment for the sin

phrases.english: For all sins in the Torah
punishment is taken from him,
but here, from him and from his family.
phrases.notes: "Here" means a false oath, the sin of לא תשא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new line of the same ברייתא that step 16 began quoting.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For other sins only the sinner is punished; for a false oath his family is punished as well.

steps.title: Other sins also punish the family
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא: the Torah says about another sin, 'I will set My face against that man and against his family.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And for all sins in the Torah, is the family not punished?! But it is written: 'Then I will set My face against that man and against his family.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the ברייתא's claim that only a false oath brings punishment on the family. It points to a פסוק about another sin where the family is punished too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא made it sound as if no other sin reaches the family. But the פסוק in ויקרא 20:5, which is about the sin of מולך, clearly mentions the sinner's משפחה. So the family being punished seems not to be unique to a false oath.

keyTerms.meaning: But it is written!, introduces a פסוק used to challenge
I will set My face against, meaning I will punish

phrases.english: And for all sins in the Torah,
is punishment not taken from his family?!
But it is written:
"Then I will set My face
against that man and against his family";
phrases.notes: ויקרא 20:5. This פסוק is about someone who serves מולך.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא line quoted in step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's claim that only for a false oath is the family punished.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק about a different sin (מולך) says the family is punished too, so this is not unique to a false oath.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: families cover for their sinners
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון explains why the family is punished in that פסוק: a family that has a crooked tax collector or a bandit is treated as guilty because they cover for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it was taught: רבי שמעון said: If he sinned, what did his family sin? This tells you that there is no family with a tax collector in it that is not all tax collectors, and with a bandit in it that is not all bandits, because they cover for him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a ברייתא to strengthen the challenge. רבי שמעון explains that the family really is punished for other sins, because they protect the sinner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might say the פסוק does not really mean the family is punished. רבי שמעון shows that it does mean it, and he even gives a reason: by covering for the sinner, the family shares in his guilt. This makes the challenge against the ברייתא even stronger.

keyTerms.meaning: A tax collector, here one who collects unfairly
They cover for him, they protect and hide him

phrases.english: And it was taught: Rabbi Shimon said:
If he sinned,
what did his family sin?
This comes to tell you:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לְךָ מִשְׁפָּחָה שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהּ מוֹכֵס –
phrases.english: there is no family that has a tax collector in it
that is not entirely tax collectors;
and none that has a bandit in it
that is not entirely bandits;
because they cover for him!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן: אִם הוּא חָטָא, מִשְׁפַּחְתּוֹ מָה חָטָאת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up the challenge of step 23 with a ברייתא that confirms and explains the family's punishment.
steps.raayaObject: That the family is punished for sins other than a false oath.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי שמעון explaining ויקרא 20:5.

steps.title: Elsewhere a different punishment, here the same punishment
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: for other sins the family gets a different punishment, but for a false oath the family gets the sinner's own punishment.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, with a different punishment; here, with his own punishment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge with a short distinction. Both cases punish the family, but not in the same way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the case of מולך, the family is punished, but with a lighter, different punishment than the sinner gets. For a false oath, the family gets the very same punishment as the sinner. So the ברייתא is still right that a false oath is more severe regarding the family.

keyTerms.meaning: With his own punishment, the same one the sinner gets

phrases.english: There, with a different punishment;
phrases.notes: "There" is מולך and other sins; "here" is a false oath.

phrases.english: here, with his own punishment;

steps.confusionAlert: The answer does not say the family goes unpunished for other sins. It agrees they are punished, just not with the sinner's own punishment.
steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם בְּדִינָא אַחֲרִינָא, הָכָא בְּדִינָא דִּידֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 23-24 by making a distinction.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: what kind of punishment the family receives.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the family is punished for other sins too, a false oath is not unique in this way.
steps.terutzMaskana: For other sins the family gets a lesser, different punishment; for a false oath they get the sinner's own punishment.

steps.title: רבי: only the sinner gets כרת
steps.stepSummary: רבי shows from the word 'אותו' (him) that for מולך only the sinner gets כרת, not his whole family. This proves the family there gets a different punishment.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: רבי says: 'And I will cut him off.' Why does the verse say this? Since it says 'Then I will set My face,' one might think the entire family gets כרת. So the verse says 'him': he gets כרת, and the entire family does not get כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove the distinction it just made. The word 'אותו' shows that in the מולך case, the family does not get the sinner's own punishment of כרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק first mentions the man and his family, and then says 'I will cut him off.' רבי explains that the word 'אותו' limits the כרת to the sinner alone. So the family's punishment for מולך must be something else, which fits the answer in step 25.

keyTerms.meaning: And I will cut him off, meaning the punishment of כרת
Why does the verse need to say this?
One might think, introduces a mistaken idea the פסוק will rule out
כרת, the punishment of being cut off

phrases.english: As it was taught: Rebbi says:
"And I will cut him off": why does the verse say this?
phrases.notes: Same פסוק as before, ויקרא 20:5.

phrases.english: Since it says:
"Then I will set My face,"
one might think the entire family gets כרת?
So the verse says: "him":
he gets כרת,
and the entire family does not get כרת.

steps.whatToRemember: For מולך the family is punished, but only the sinner gets כרת. For a false oath the family shares the sinner's own punishment, which is why that sin is so severe.
steps.triggerLanguage: כִּדְתַנְיָא, רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: ״וְהִכְרַתִּי אוֹתוֹ״ – מָה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the distinction made in step 25.
steps.raayaObject: That for other sins the family gets a different punishment, not the sinner's own.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי's teaching on 'אותו' in ויקרא 20:5, limiting כרת to the sinner.

steps.title: For a false oath, the whole world is punished
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: for other sins only the sinner is punished, but for a false oath the whole world is punished, based on פסוקים in הושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: For all other sins in the Torah, only the sinner is punished. Here, he and the whole world are punished. The פסוק says 'swearing and lying,' and right after it says 'therefore the land mourns.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the ברייתא. It adds one more way a false oath is worse than other sins: its punishment reaches the whole world.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the ברייתא said the sinner's family is punished too. Now it goes further: the whole world suffers. The proof is that הושע lists 'swearing' and then says the land mourns.

phrases.english: And for all sins in the Torah, punishment is taken from him,
but here, from him and from the entire world;
as it is said: 'Swearing and lying,'
phrases.notes: הושע 4:2

phrases.english: and it is written: 'Therefore the land mourns.'
phrases.notes: הושע 4:3

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the same ברייתא after the discussion of the family's punishment.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A false oath brings punishment on the sinner and the entire world, unlike other sins.

steps.title: Maybe only if he does all the listed sins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the land only mourns if the person commits every sin listed in the פסוק, not just the false oath.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe say it only happens when he does all of them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pokes at the proof from הושע. The פסוק lists several sins together, so maybe the land mourns only when all of them are done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in הושע names swearing, lying, murder, stealing and adultery together. So the proof is weak: maybe the world is punished only for the whole list, not for a false oath alone.

phrases.english: But say: not until he does all of them!
phrases.notes: 'All of them' means all the sins listed together in that פסוק in הושע.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof פסוק brought in step 27.
steps.kashyaTarget: The proof from הושע that a false oath alone brings punishment on the world.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק lists many sins together, so the punishment may depend on doing all of them.

steps.title: A false oath alone makes the land mourn
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers from ירמיהו, where the land mourns because of swearing alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: Don't think that, because it says: 'Because of swearing the land mourns.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by bringing a different פסוק. This one mentions only swearing as the reason the land mourns.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ירמיהו there is no list of other sins, only 'swearing.' So a false oath by itself is enough to bring suffering on the land, and the ברייתא's rule stands.

keyTerms.meaning: don't let that enter your mind

steps.whatToRemember: A false oath alone, without any other sins, is enough to bring punishment on the whole land.

phrases.english: It should not enter your mind,
as it is written: 'Because of swearing the land mourns.'
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 23:10

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 28.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The land mourns only when all the sins in הושע are done together.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק in ירמיהו shows swearing alone makes the land mourn.

steps.title: Aren't all Jews responsible for each other's sins?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא: a פסוק teaches that all ישראל are guarantors for each other, so the whole world should be punished for every sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: For all other sins, isn't the whole world punished? The פסוק says 'they will stumble one man on his brother,' meaning one through his brother's sin. This teaches that all ישראל are guarantors for one another!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the ברייתא's claim that only a false oath brings punishment on everyone. A פסוק seems to say every sin does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said other sins are punished only on the sinner. But ויקרא is read to mean one Jew stumbles because of another's sin, since all ישראל are guarantors. If so, a false oath is not special in this way.
steps.confusionAlert: The word 'world' here is being challenged by a teaching about כל ישראל. The question is not about non-Jews; it is whether everyone, not just the sinner, is punished for other sins.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the famous source for the idea that all ישראל are responsible for one another.

phrases.english: And for all other sins in the Torah –
is the whole world not punished?!
But isn't it written: 'And they shall stumble one man on his brother' –
phrases.notes: ויקרא 26:37

phrases.english: one man because of his brother's sin;

phrases.aramaic: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁכׇּל יִשְׂרָאֵל עֲרֵבִים זֶה בָּזֶה!
phrases.english: this teaches that all Israel are guarantors for one another!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכׇל עֲבֵירוֹת שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה מִכׇּל הָעוֹלָם לָא? וְהָכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ברייתא's rule from step 27 and challenges its contrast between a false oath and other sins.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's statement that for other sins only the sinner is punished.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק teaches that all ישראל are guarantors for one another, so every sin should bring punishment on others too.
